newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway oil union to start mediated talks on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Norway oil union to start mediated talks on Friday.

text.p: The Federation of Norwegian Oil Workers (OFS) will meet with the Norwegian shipowners' organisation NR on Friday to try to save this year's wage negotiations and avert a strike at floating production installations, a union official said on Tuesday.
OFS first deputy Bjoern Tjessem said the two sides met with the state-appointed mediator on Monday to discuss the progress of talks.

"There has been no movement in the situation. We will begin negotiations again at 12 o'clock (1000 GMT) on Friday, and if there is no progress by the deadline then there could be a strike," Tjessem told Reuters.
Deadline for discussions is midnight on Saturday.
"We can decide to say 'yes' to what's on the table at midnight or we can say 'no'. We are working as if there is a danger of a strike," Tjessem said.
OFS has 800 members on 20 floating systems on the Norwegian continental shelf.
Tjessem said the union's central committee would meet on Wednesday to decided if all workers on the installations would be brought out at once or if action would be phased in.

Industrial action would not immediately affect oil production on the Norwegian continental shelf, but a prolonged strike could result in the shutdown of some oil and gas output and also would affect exploration and drilling activity and other support functions.

OFS broke off talks with NR at the end of June due to disagreements over a rise in the minimum wage for managers with individual salary agreements, completion of a harmonisation in terms covering workers on fixed and floating installations, and pension terms.

Unions are required by Norwegian law to undertake a period of state-mediated talks with employers with a set deadline. If no solution is agreed in those talks, then unions are free to strike as soon as the deadline has passed.
